recipes.name: PHILADELPHIA® Fruit Pizza
ingredients_raw: 1 (16.5 ounce) package refrigerated sliceable sugar cookies, sliced
1 (8 ounce) package PHILADELPHIA Cream Cheese, softened
4 cups assorted cut-up fruit (kiwi, strawberries, blueberries, drained canned mandarin oranges)
0.25 cup apricot preserves, pressed through sieve to remove lumps

steps.text: Line 12-inch pizza pan with foil; spray with cooking spray. Arrange cookie dough slices in single layer in prepared pan; press together to form crust. Bake 14 min.; cool completely. Invert onto plate; carefully remove foil. Turn crust over.
Beat cream cheese, sugar and vanilla with mixer until well blended. Spread over crust.
Top with fruit. Mix preserves and water; brush over fruit. Refrigerate 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: PHILADELPHIA® Fruit Pizza
raw_recipe.description: On a baked cookie 'crust,' arrange sliced kiwi, berries and mandarin orange segments on a creamy layer of 'sauce' for a pretty summer dessert.

review.reviewBody: Yum! Great flavors--I added vanilla bean to the cream cheese mixture. Also, did individual-sized by slicing cookie dough, placing in lined muffin pans and baking as directed. Worked wonderfully and was a great hit! Fruits I used were blueberries, kiwi, strawberry, and mandarin oranges. Will post photo. PS: I have made with orange marmalade in the past, which works as well as apricot. Gives such a nice sheen to enhance the appearance.

have made this many x over the years, it is ALWAYS loved by everyone. I used to make my home made sugar cookie recipe for the crust, but have switched to the store bought logs, rolled out, since no one can seem to tell the difference. Its just easier. Always seem to use the same fruit combo, strawberry, blueberry, mandarine oranges, pineapple. Have tried it both ways as far as the glazing on top, seems that it does better for me without it. Also, the crust can become soggy, so I bake the cookie crust a little more brown, to hold up better, & drain & lay wetter fruits, [ mandarine oranges, canned pineapple etc ] on a paper towel before adding to the top, to dry them off a bit.

This made a great impression! So easy. I debated rolling the dough out or cutting it into cookies and then laying it in the pizza pan. Cutting the cookies was the way to go. Easier to press the dough together and be sure it will cover the pan evenly. Also pack as much fruit as you can to make it pretty and fruity. I could’ve put more fruit on it and it would’ve looked a bit better. I only had a 14” pizza pan so I added another 4 oz of cream cheese a dash more sugar and vanilla. It looks like you slaved but it’s so easy!

My husband,who is very picky about eating fruit and my kids loved this recipe. I actually added 1/2 tsp of cinnamon to the cream cheese mixture and it turned out good. Also instead of the break away cookies i just used the sugar cookie roll and flattened it out into a circle. Great snack for kids though!

Wonderful and tasty. Had this for guests and they all loved it!
I made them as individual cookies, which was so easy . No plating of dessert. One recommendation would be to make sure to use plenty of the cream cheese frosting on the edges as that’s will make the fruit stick on. Will definitely make again. If you make it as individual cookies, allow for prep time as its kind of putsy.

Fruit Pizza is a family favorite, but I try to keep it simple. I use a disposable, foil pan, if I am taking this to a BBQ and put it in a pizza box. The directions here seem a little time consuming, lining the pan with foil, flipping the whole thing and straining the marmalade. I just melt a little apple jelly to brush on mine to make the fruit all shiny. Great recipe!

I love philly fruit pizza! I made mine with Pillsbury Pet Ritz pie crust, flattened down on a pizza stone. Then I used 1/3 less fat philly cream cheese to make a bit healthier. Jersey peaches and blueberries with mandarin oranges...it looks like an orange flower!
I made these in mini muffin tins and they were AMAZING and so easy. Everyone was so impressed at a bridal shower- I used blueberries and strawberries.

excited to post my photo of this recipe before even tasting it because it's so easy, and easy to make beautiful. I added almond extract instead of vanilla; I imagine orange extract and/or peel would also compliment these flavors. Instead of water in the preserves, I used the light syrup drained from the mandarin oranges.

My first fruit pizza. Turned out great. Decorated it with strawberries, blueberries, and bananas for a 4th of July cookout. It was s big hit. Got rave reviews. First dessert gone! Will definitely be making again. Can use with all kinds of seasonal fruits! Thanks for a great recipe.
It’s easy enough and fool proof and beautiful and delicious. I’ve made it as written at least 5 times. Always a hit.
I've made this several times and with many different fruit combinations. For me it's a no-fail recipe and always is so good. My family, ranging from 9 to 72, all love it. Thanks for the great recipe!
Winter time is a challenge to find nice tasting fresh fruit. I used canned mandarin oranges and canned pineapple, cherry pie filling and fresh blueberries. It all tastes great!
I will make this again, it was very fresh!
Pretty yummy. I added a splash of heavy cream (whipped cream would work) to the topping to lighten it up.
Awesome! Will definitley be making this again!

I did not use the preserves and put on the fruit I wanted in the desired amounts and I baked on a large cookie sheet. Baking time was the same. I also didn’t use foil and just greased the cookie sheet. The rest I followed and oh man was this fabulous! Sooo good!
I would cut back on the sugar added to the cream cheese
I made the recipe with a slight change, I added cool whip to the cream cheese and took out the sugar. It was Perfect! my husband said it reminded him of a German torte.
